author: GamingBolt
description:
Windrose is a recently released early access title that presents the player with in-depth survival mechanics, dressed up in the guise of a pirate game. It really feels like it could benefit greatly from more development time, but as of right now, it offers a solid foundation for what could one day be a phenomenal pirate game.

Instead of being a quick fix, Windrose will feel more rewarding to patient players who are willing to take a chance on an ambitious, debut project from a fresh development studio. If you are looking to boot up and be sailing to the far ends of the high seas within a few hours of gameplay, then Windrose may not satiate you. It lacks flair in its current state, but the game at least knows what it wants to be, even if it isn’t quite there yet.
title: Windrose Early Access Review - The Next BIG Pirate Game?

author: GamingBolt
description:
Some may find appeal in the boundlessness of space – a sandbox of potentially infinite possibilities, depending on how you want to make your own fun. But there's a reason that games like Mass Effect have remained so beloved for so long. Space isn't just a place of freedom, but another frontier for storytelling, carried by memorable companions, and defined by your choices and consequences. Call them limits, if you will, but living that life and forming a core part of the narrative backbone is something that sci-fi RPG fans continue to crave.

Thus, we come to The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. It's uncharted territory for Owlcat Games. Going from tactical real-time-with-pause and turn-based combat into a real-time, cover-based shooter is one thing. Add on the established universe and lore of The Expanse, which has its own dedicated following in sci-fi circles, and the potential risk feels doubled.
title: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn Is the Mass Effect Successor You've Been Waiting For [NEW GAMEPLAY]

author: GamingBolt
description:
Pragmata is doing very well since its release, and if you’ve been keeping up with the discourse around it, it’s easy to see why. It’s got a great story, solid combat, and enough charm to make you invested in Hugh and Diana’s budding friendship. But in a game that’s decidedly short compared to its peers, how has Pragmata managed to keep its players coming back for more? 

We think it’s because the developer focused on quality over quantity, making an experience that stands out because it doesn’t obligate players to see it through. Instead, they keep diving back in because it’s plain old fun. In a game this polished, that can quickly become a reason for many players to engage with The Cradle’s mechanics. Join us as we examine how a focused experience might be one of Pragmata’s biggest strengths.
title: Why Are Millions Addicted To Pragmata?
